title: 🤖 Web: Handle text from input methods that don't compose
body:
> [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by an autonomous AI agent (Claude Code), on behalf of a user, to fix text input in their Godot web export. The agent diagnosed the issue, wrote the patch and this description; the user tested the fix in their browser.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

On the web platform, text typed through an input method that commits characters directly (without composition events) never reaches `LineEdit`/`TextEdit`. No existing issue found.

**Reproduction:** Ubuntu (GNOME, Wayland) with IBus and a Russian layout, Chrome or Firefox, any web export with a focused `LineEdit`: Latin letters type, Cyrillic letters don't. The browser sends `keydown` with `key == "Process"` (`keyCode == 229`) and delivers the character only in an `input` event (`inputType == "insertText"`) on the focused IME element. Most mobile virtual keyboards use the same pattern.

## Additional information

**Cause:** the IME element (`GodotIME`) forwards every keydown to the engine (as the raw key `"Process"`, which carries no unicode), calls `preventDefault()`, and only listens to composition events, so the text is dropped.

**Fix:** keydowns that belong to the input method (`isComposing`, `keyCode == 229`, `"Process"`, `"Unidentified"`) are left to the browser, and `insertText` input events are committed like a finished composition (start + commit), which `DisplayServerWeb` already turns into unicode key events. Normal keys and composition-based IMEs should be unaffected.

**Tested:** a 4.7.1-based web export (a minimal project with `LineEdit` + `TextEdit`) on Ubuntu (GNOME, Wayland) with IBus: Cyrillic now types; and on a phone browser with its virtual keyboard: Latin and Cyrillic typing and Backspace work. **Not tested:** CJK IMEs.
